correctness.rationale: The distinguished direction of a flex one-cell from sink to source makes the constant one-cochain a cocycle on all squares. Each circular component has, by Kozlov Theorem 6.1, a primitive n-edge core circle traversed entirely by sink flips; the cochain pairs to n on the generator, so this uniquely fixes the positive integral generator. An automorphism preserves this cochain while total arrow reversal sends it to its negative; naturality forces exactly the signed permutation module, integrally. Rational transfer/invariants on a finite quotient gives the stated orbit-stabilizer formula. The independent standard-library program checked 18 graphs, complete GF(2) first-homology ranks, all square boundary cancellations, 48 circular components, 582 symmetry/core instances, and all recorded expectations. Limits are explicit.

value.rationale: A complete integral equivariant first-homology representation across all finite connected graphs supplies a canonical primitive winding class in each circle component, distinguishes automorphism and global direction-reversal actions, and settles the first rational Betti number of every subgroup quotient via a sharp stabilizer condition. This is a natural general structural invariant of Kozlov’s newly defined reconfiguration complexes; unlike a finite example or a renamed homology rank, it gives uniform symmetry and quotient information previously only computed for complete graphs.
